content: 1. For immunocompetent patients, the preferred regimen includes Ampicillin-Sulbactam at a dose of 2 grams administered intravenously every 4 hours. Alternatively, Clindamycin at 600 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours can also be used. 2. For immunocompromised patients, the preferred regimens are as follows: Cefotaxime at 2 grams intravenously every 6 hours. Ceftizoxime at 4 grams intravenously every 8 hours. Piperacillin at 3 grams intravenously every 4 hours. Imipenem at 500 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours. Meropenem at 1 gram intravenously every 8 hours. Gatifloxacin at 400 milligrams intravenously every 24 hours. 3. For acute laryngitis, antibiotics are not recommended as they do not significantly improve objective symptoms. 4. For diphtheria, the CDC recommends: Erythromycin (oral or intravenous) for 14 days at a dose of 40 milligrams per kilogram per day, with a maximum of 2 grams per day. Procaine penicillin G administered intramuscularly for 14 days at a dose of 300,000 units per day for patients weighing less than 10 kilograms. 5. For sinusitis in pediatric patients with treatment failure, a culture should be performed to guide therapy. In the absence of cultures, or if the child fails Amoxicillin, the following regimens are recommended: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate (extra strength) suspension at 90 milligrams per kilogram per day (amoxicillin component) orally, divided every 12 hours for 10–14 days. Clindamycin at 30–40 milligrams per kilogram per day divided every 8 hours, combined with a third-generation cephalosporin such as Cefuroxime axetil at 30 milligrams per kilogram per day orally, divided every 12 hours. Preferred regimens include Cefdinir at 14 milligrams per kilogram per day orally, divided every 12 or 24 hours, or Cefpodoxime at 10 milligrams per kilogram per day orally, divided every 12 hours. 6. For sinusitis in adults with treatment failure after 7 days of diagnosis, the preferred regimens are: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate at 4 grams per day of amoxicillin equivalent. Levofloxacin at 500 milligrams orally once daily. Moxifloxacin at 400 milligrams orally once daily. 7. For stomatitis (aphthous ulcers), topical steroids may reduce pain and swelling. 8. For herpetic stomatitis, Acyclovir at 15 milligrams per kilogram orally every 5 hours for 7 days is recommended. 9. For submandibular space infections, including Ludwig’s angina, the causative pathogens include viridans streptococci, Peptostreptococcus, Bacteroides, and other oral anaerobes. The preferred regimens for immunocompetent patients are: Penicillin G at 2–4 million units intravenously every 4–6 hours combined with Tobramycin at 2 milligrams per kilogram intravenously every 8 hours. Ampicillin-Sulbactam at 2 grams intravenously every 4 hours. Clindamycin at 600 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours. Doxycycline at 200 milligrams intravenously every 12 hours. Cefoxitin at 2 grams intravenously every 6 hours. Cefotetan at 2 grams intravenously every 12 hours. 10. For immunocompromised patients with submandibular space infections, the preferred regimens include: Cefotaxime at 2 grams intravenously every 6 hours. Ceftizoxime at 4 grams intravenously every 8 hours. Piperacillin at 3 grams intravenously every 4 hours. Imipenem at 500 milligrams intravenously every 6 hours. Meropenem at 1 gram intravenously every 8 hours. Gatifloxacin at 200 milligrams intravenously every 24 hours. 11. For tonsillitis, the preferred regimen is Penicillin V orally for 10 days. If compliance is unlikely, a single dose of intramuscular Benzathine penicillin can be administered. Alternate regimens include: Second-generation cephalosporins orally for 4–6 days. Clindamycin or Azithromycin for 5 days. Clarithromycin for 10 days. Erythromycin for 10 days. 12. For Vincent’s angina, the preferred treatment is Penicillin G at 4 million units intravenously every 4 hours. An alternate treatment is Clindamycin at 600 milligrams intravenously every 8 hours.
